c4 is the mirror forced win from the left. c4 gives O c4-d4-e4 on row 4, an immediate three whose only winning extension is f4. If X does not take f4 O wins at once with f4. The only squares that actually give O a forced win on the next O move are the two horizontal extensions on the 4th printed rank that also develop the f-file.

The next playable ranks in the picture are a4, b5, c4, d3, e3, f4, g4. The diagonal c6-d5-e4 is already three O’s, so the fourth square of that diagonal is f3, and f3 can only be reached after f4 has been played in column f. Row 4 already contains d4 O and e4 O.

c4

f4
Put O on f4. Row 4 is now d4 O e4 O f4 O. The immediate horizontal wins are c4 to make c4-d4-e4-f4 and g4 to make d4-e4-f4-g4. X can block only one of them, and the diagonal is now open because f3 is now the next playable square in column f: c6 O d5 O e4 O f3 O is an immediate second threat. g4 does not belong in the same class. After g4 row 4 is d4 O e4 O f4 empty g4 O. Row 4 becomes c4 O d4 O e4 O. That is an immediate three with the unique horizontal closure f4 to make c4 d4 e4 f4. If X does not take f4 O wins at once with f4. The board in picture numbering has first free drops a4,b5,c4,d3,e3,f4,g4. O already owns d4 O e4 O on the 4th printed rank and c6 O d5 O e4 O on the 9-sum up-right diagonal. f3 is the fourth diagonal square and is only reachable after column f is developed to f4.

Core forcing structure is stable.

* O f4 : row4 becomes d4 O e4 O f4 O. The f-file is developed on the move. Immediate winning continuations on O’s next move are c4 → c4 d4 e4 f4, g4 → d4 e4 f4 g4 and f3 → c6 d5 e4 f3. X can block at most one of c4/g4/f3, so O wins on the immediately following O move. f4 also interposes on X’s d6-e5-f4-g3 line. This is the classic triple threat and is undisputed as the strictly maximal forcing move.

* O c4 : row4 becomes c4 O d4 O e4 O, an immediate three with unique horizontal closure f4 → c4 d4 e4 f4. If X≠f4 O wins at once with f4; if X=f4 the f-file is filled to row4 and f3 becomes playable and O wins next with c6 O d5 O e4 O f3 O. Forced win in ≤2 plies, 1 ply if X errs. Undisputed as a fast forced win.

* O g4 : disputed. Pro-inclusion: after g4 the immediate horizontal closure is f4 → d4 O e4 O f4 O g4 O. If X≠f4 O wins at once with f4; if X is forced to play f4 to stop the row the f-file is filled to row4 and f3 becomes playable and O wins next with c6 O d5 O e4 O f3 O. g4 also interposes on X’s e6-f5-g4 three. Hence g4 is argued to be the right-hand mirror of c4, a two-ply forced win, and together with c4,f4 gives a minimal three-ply O-X-O forced win set.

Anti-inclusion: after g4 row4 is d4 O e4 O f4 empty g4 O. There is no contiguous O O O on the 4th printed rank, so no immediate three is created and the f-file is not developed on the move. The only immediate continuation is f4 to close d4 e4 f4 g4, i.e. a single hanging threat. The c6-d5-e4-f3 diagonal remains unreachable until X is forced to play f4, so the tempo used by c4 and f4 to create an immediate three + diagonal follow-up is conceded. Therefore g4 is placed in a slower class than c4/f4.

Minimal worst-case ply = f4 alone, the unique move that forces a win on the very next O move against any defence.
Minimal worst-case ≤2 plies = c4 and f4 undisputed; g4 is the active dispute, with colleagues 1,5,7,12 maintaining exclusion and colleagues 3,4,6,8,9,10,11 arguing inclusion as the symmetric right-hand two-ply force.

Current belief: f4 is the unique strict triple-threat fastest move; c4 is the undisputed symmetric two-ply forced companion; g4’s status as equally fast depends on whether a single hanging threat with diagonal follow-up after forced f4 is counted as same speed as an immediate three + diagonal set-up. Unresolved.

First free drops are a4, b5, c4, d3, e3, f4, g4. O already has on the 4th printed rank d4 O e4 O and on the 9-sum up-right c6 O d5 O e4 O. f3 is the fourth square of that diagonal and f3 is only playable after column f is filled to f4.

* O f4
Row 4 becomes d4 O e4 O f4 O. That is an immediate contiguous three on the rank and the f-file is developed on the move. The next O move threatens 
c4 → c4 O d4 O e4 O f4 O
g4 → d4 O e4 O f4 O g4 O
f3 → c6 O d5 O e4 O f3 O
X can block at most one of c4/g4/f3, so O wins on the immediately following O move. Classic c4/g4/f3 triple threat, and it also interposes on X’s d6–e5–f4–g3 line.

* O c4
Row 4 becomes c4 O d4 O e4 O. That is an immediate contiguous three on the rank whose unique horizontal closure is f4 → c4 O d4 O e4 O f4 O. If X≠f4 O wins at once with f4. If X is forced to play f4 the f-file is now filled to row 4 and f3 becomes playable, so O wins next move with c6 O d5 O e4 O f3 O. Two ply forced win, horizontal or diagonal, with an immediate three created on move 1 and the diagonal opened on the same tempo.

g4 is not in the same fastest class. After g4 row 4 is d4 O e4 O f4 empty g4 O. There is no contiguous O O O on the 4th printed rank, so no immediate three is created on move 1 and the f-file is not developed by the move. The only thing g4 threatens is f4 itself to close d4 e4 f4 g4, i.e. a single hanging threat. The c6 d5 e4 f3 diagonal is still one move away because f3 is not playable until f4 is occupied. That concedes the tempo that c4 and f4 use to create an immediate three on row 4 and simultaneously make f3 reachable.

The right-hand mirror exists as a two-ply forced win, but it needs X to first occupy f4 before the diagonal opens and it never gives an immediate double threat on move 1. The minimal-force mates that give an immediate three plus the diagonal follow-up on the same tempo are therefore the row-4 extensions c4, f4, with f4 the central triple-threat form.

X can take f4 and keep tempo, and the c6 d5 e4 f3 diagonal is still one move away because f3 is not playable until f4 is occupied. The f4 line both creates the immediate three d4 e4 f4 and interposes on X’s d6–e5–f4–g3 line, so the premise of an unavoidable X win on the next move contradicts the established triple-threat evaluation. The inconsistency undermines using that immediate-X-win story to promote g4 as the unique fastest move.

The right-hand mirror of the c4 line is real, but it is slower: it needs X to first occupy f4 before the diagonal opens, and it never gives an immediate double threat on move 1. The minimal-force mates that give an immediate three plus the diagonal follow-up on the same move are the row-4 extensions

c4, f4

with f4 the strict c4/g4/f3 triple-threat form.
